*** IT IS SATURDAY. EVERY INSTRUMENT BUT BITCOIN CARRIES FRIDAY'S CLOSE. ***
Equities, both bond markets, oil and the FX pairs are all shut, so the ticker shows Friday 2 October's
closing levels with FRIDAY'S changes. Bitcoin is the only instrument trading, and its change is today's.
This is stated here because a reader comparing the Saturday ticker with Friday evening's will see small
differences: the evening edition carried LIVE intraday values at 18:13, and several instruments moved
between then and the close. Specifically:
  Gold  published Friday evening at 4,138.43 (-0.94%) live; CLOSED 4,142.34, so Friday's move was -0.85%
  VIX   published Friday evening at 15.73 (-0.06%) live;  CLOSED 15.31, so Friday's move was -6.59%
  S&P   published Friday evening at 7,723.31 (+0.74%) live; CLOSED 7,722.72, +0.73%
  Brent published Friday evening at 102.39 (+0.08%) live;  SETTLED 102.25, so Friday's move was -0.06%
None of those evening figures was wrong — they were correct for 18:13 — but the closes supersede them
and the Saturday edition carries the closes.

*** GILT: PROVIDERS DISAGREE ON THE SIGN AGAIN, AND IT DOES NOT MATTER THIS TIME ***
CNBC has Friday's ten-year close at 5.3770% against a Thursday close of 5.3721%, i.e. +0.005.
Trading Economics says the ten-year "eased to 5.38% on October 2, 2026, marking a 0.01 percentage points
decrease". So the two disagree on direction by about one basis point, as they did on 1 October.
DECISION: publish 5.38 with +0.01, which is exactly what this site published on Friday evening. Because
the gilt market has not opened since, Friday's close IS Friday evening's figure, so republishing it
unchanged is the only internally consistent answer and no new adjudication is required. The published
series for the week therefore reads: 5.38 -> 5.44 -> 5.48 -> 5.39 -> 5.37 -> 5.38 -> 5.38.
THE THIRTY-YEAR: CNBC has it at 5.8840% and Trading Economics at 5.91%, a wider gap than the ten-year.
The standing rule from 1 October applies — no daily direction is asserted for the thirty-year, and the
impact box says only that it is well below the 6.0289% it touched on Thursday, which both providers agree.

*** BRENT: FIFTH DAY ON THE DECEMBER CONTRACT ***
@LCO.1 remains Dec'26 and settled at 102.25. Wednesday evening's published 103.62 was NOVEMBER and is
still not comparable; the driver says so for the fifth edition running, per the standing rule. The December
contract's own week: 98.03 settle on Wednesday, 102.31 Thursday, 102.25 Friday — so the G7 reserve
announcement on Friday afternoon did not move it materially either way.

THE WEEK, IN ONE LINE: gilts spiked to a 28-year high on Thursday and gave it all back; the FTSE lost
1.68% on Thursday and recovered 0.32% on Friday; diesel broke £2 a litre; and the G7 opened its reserves.
The VIX ending the week at 15.31, down 6.59% on the day, is the clearest single sign the scare has passed.
